title: ioctl_init: algo empty check after forced null-termination is off-by-one
description: In ioctl_init(), the code does: op.algo[CRYPTO2DEV_ALGO_MAXLEN - 1] = '\0' then checks 'if (op.algo[0] == 0) return -EINVAL'. This is correct. However: if the user passes an algo string that is exactly CRYPTO2DEV_ALGO_MAXLEN bytes with no null terminator (all 64 bytes are non-null), after the forced null-termination, op.algo[63] is overwritten with '\0'. The effective algo string is truncated to 63 chars. This truncation happens silently — the algo_lookup will then look for the truncated name. If the intended algo name was exactly 64 chars (no terminator), the user gets -ENOENT instead of -EINVAL. This is a minor AX issue: the UAPI says algo is 'null-terminated' so a 64-byte non-null string is malformed input. However, the error returned (-ENOENT from lookup vs -EINVAL for bad input) is misleading. Same issue exists in ioctl_key_import and ioctl_key_generate. Trigger: pass algo[63]='x' with all 64 bytes non-null → gets silently truncated to 63 chars → -ENOENT rather than -EINVAL. Not a safety issue but a UAPI contract violation.
close_reason: false positive: algo empty check is correct in all three functions; tp5.46/tp5.47 P0 fixes added the check to key_import/key_generate; ioctl_init already had it
